title: Clarify SGI as an institutional capability with an operating model
requirements:
- State at the start of Appendix F that SGI is an institutional and operational framework supported by tools, not a single software platform
- Describe the recurrent staffing, tooling, licensing and translation costs of maintaining semantic assets after first publication
- State where SGI decisions sit relative to strategic and operational governance and the 3.4.4 escalation path
- Give governance models and responsibilities, drawing on WHO-FIC and HL7 experience
- State prominently that SGI is a governance capability supported by tools, or consider a name without 'infrastructure'
- Explain how ministries, architecture teams, terminology centres and procurement teams use the catalogue (assessment, target design, role assignment)
- Give indicative minimum staffing patterns and options for regional pooling of semantic governance
- Relate the governance/runtime/content layers to the architecture framework used elsewhere in the document
